Exposure swept 2026-09-15 at 00:00:01:09; Temperature and Contrast at 00:00:01:08, hence the small differences between the two zero rows (a different frame, not drift). contrast._p10p90Removed: REMOVED 2026-09-17. These arrays were physically impossible: p10 sat BELOW p1 on all seven rows (8.6 against 11.4 at neutral, 17.0 against 18.4 at -100), and the 10th percentile cannot be under the 1st. They were another frame's numbers (C193 @15.39) merged into this block, part extrapolated and part interpolated, with nothing flagging it. With them gone the fallback takes over and interpolates p10/p90 from the frame's own p1/p50/p99. The removed values are kept here only so nobody re-derives them: p10 [17.0, 13.0, 10.6, 8.6, 7.1, 4.9, 1.9], p90 [71.7, 74.7, 76.5, 77.6, 79.2, 81.0, 84.0].

curveToe._source: Live curve_sweep 2026-09-17 17:05, C220 (A056_05072232_C220.braw) at 0.5 s on the [AI] copy - the SAME frame wheelBands was fitted on (its `neutral` row: p1 8.2, p99 75.7, blacksRB -1.6), so the two blocks are comparable. The Master curve's bottom point at each x, identity elsewhere, the clip's own curves restored after. Answers the question both reverted blue-blacks attempts guessed at: what a bottom-point move at x does to each channel's floor.
curveToe._model: CONFIRMED: the published levels line. A channel at level `in` lands at (in - 100x)/(1 - x), floored at 0. Measured against every unclamped row: within 0.6 IRE and ALWAYS a touch high (the soft toe), which is what blackInFor's own note already said. So ~1.0 IRE of fall per 0.01 of x, and blackInFor/predictLevels need no correction.
curveToe._rigid: THE FINDING THAT MATTERS: the toe moves all three channels by the SAME amount. Red-minus-blue spacing across the rows is 4.70 -> 4.80 -> 4.30 (the last already clamping) against a starting 4.70. The Master bottom point is a rigid translation of the parade, so it CANNOT close a gap between the channel floors - it can only push the whole parade down until the lowest channel clamps. The blue blacks are a SPACING defect and the black point is the wrong knob for them; only per-channel toes (neutralBottoms) change spacing.
curveToe._bandBlind: AND THE TRAP: bands.blacks EXCLUDES any pixel with a channel at 0 or 255 (src/scopes.cjs, the `r > 0 && g > 0 && b > 0` guard). So its blacksRB drift here (-1.6 -> -1.2 -> 0 -> +1.6 -> +2 -> null) is NOT a cast the toe created - it is survivorship, the sample shrinking as blue crushes out of it, and at x=0.2 the band is empty. Rule: bands.blacks is only trustworthy while the floor shares are ~0. Reading it after a deep black point - which is exactly what the correction passes do - reads a biased subset.
curveToe._usable: On this frame the toe is usable to x=0.05 (luma p1 8.2 -> 3.9, target 4) and no further: blue's own p1 is 4.7, so x > 0.047 puts it on the floor - 0.92% of the frame at 0.05, 5.76% at 0.1, 16.69% at 0.15. The existing cap at the lowest channel's bottom is therefore right, and tight.
curveToe._modelCORRECTION: CORRECTION 2026-09-18 21:16: `_model` holds for the LOWEST channel of the frame and for each channel curve on its own (`channelToeRedC202`, `channelToeGreenC202`, `channelToe`), and does NOT hold for the Master curve on the other channels: on C187 green reads 15.7 where the line says crushed (`curveToeAnchoredC187`), on C202 +2.9 at 0.12 (`curveToeAnchoredC202`). C220, where `_model` was fitted, has its three p1s within 4.7 IRE of each other, which is why the excess was 0.6 there. Master is not three identical channel curves; its form is unmeasured until the per-pixel map is read.
curveToe._anchoredC202: 2026-09-18 21:11, `curveToeAnchoredC202`: on C202 the anchored line holds for RED and BLUE at every bottom point (within 0.3) and NOT for GREEN (+1.0 at 0.05, +1.9 at 0.09, +2.9 at 0.12; at 0.15 green reads 2.4 where the line says crushed). Not a rounded corner - the miss is by channel, not by gap. A contradiction on record; three sweeps queued to place it (Green alone, Red alone, Master on C187).
curveToe._anchored: Swept again 2026-09-17 19:19 WITH the anchor the grade actually writes (pinned at the median 0.5 and at 0.8, a four-point spline) and it is the same curve for the black end: luma p1 8.2 / 6.7 / 4.3 / 0.4 / 0 / 0 against the unanchored 8.2 / 6.7 / 3.9 / 0.4 / 0 / 0. predictLevels' anchored form predicts it to within 0.24. So the anchor changes the midtones, not the black point, and it is not a source of model error.
curveToe._rigidCORRECTED: CORRECTION 2026-09-17: `_rigid` says the Master toe is 'a rigid translation' that 'cannot close a gap between the channel floors'. The conclusion is right and the mechanism stated for it is wrong. (v - 100x)/(1 - x) is a GAIN about 100, so it EXPANDS the spacing by 1/(1 - x) - and `_rigid`'s own numbers show it: red-minus-blue 4.70 -> 4.80 at x=0.02 is exactly 4.70/0.98, which the note reported as the spacing having 'held'. So the Master toe does not leave a cast alone, it widens it slightly, and it still cannot be used to CLOSE one. Read the conclusion, not the reason.

channelToe._source: Live curve_sweep 2026-09-17 17:15, C220 @0.5s on the [AI] copy - the same frame as curveToe and wheelBands. The BLUE curve's bottom point at each x, Master and the other channels left at identity. This is the move neutralBottoms makes, and it is precondition (b) for wiring it: curveToe measured the Master curve, which is a rigid translation and cannot do this job.
channelToe._model: CONFIRMED on the PAIRED statistic, and tighter than Master's: blue's paired bottom (7.8 at x=0) lands where (in - 100x)/(1 - x) says to within 0.15 IRE across every row - 5.9 vs 5.92, 3.1 vs 2.95, 0 vs 0. A band median is a steadier statistic than a percentile, which is why this beats curveToe's 0.6. blackInFor needs no per-channel correction.
channelToe._isolation: A channel toe moves EXACTLY ONE CHANNEL. pairedRed 10.2 and pairedGreen 8.6 are identical on all six rows while blue goes 7.8 -> 0, and the independent redP1 9.4 / greenP1 7.8 never move either. So the band's pixel selection does not shift under the move and neutralBottoms' three toes compose exactly: fed this frame's 10.2/8.6/7.8 it writes red x=0.026, green x=0.0087, blue 0, and all three land at 7.80.
channelToe._crushCap: The crush is governed by the channel's OWN p1, not its paired median. At x=0.05 blue's paired bottom is still 3.1 - healthy - while blue's own p1 is 0.4 and 0.91% of the frame is on the floor. floorBlue by blueP1: 2.7 -> 0.02%, 0.4 -> 0.91%, 0 -> 5.9%. So the cap on a channel toe is x <= (ownP1 - 2) / 98, keeping that channel's own p1 at or above ~2. neutralBottoms' flat 0.12 cap is unrelated to any of this and far too loose.
channelToe._readable: The survivorship trap of curveToe `_bandBlind`, now visible as a number: readable falls 100 -> 100 -> 80 -> 35 -> 5 -> 0 as blue crushes, and blacksRB slides -1.6 -> -10.6 with it, while the LEVELS stay exact throughout. Drive the fix from levels; treat blacksRB as unusable below ~80% readable.
channelToe._caution: C220 @0.5s has WARM blacks (paired B-R = -2.4), so this sweep exercised the mechanism in the wrong direction for the product bug. It proves the arithmetic, not the cure. The cure is judged on the 00:00:09:10 frame, where blue's floor reportedly sits ~+8 above red - and that reading is from a PARADE, i.e. independent percentiles, the exact statistic that misled 0.1.80. Check the paired levels there before wiring anything.

channelLift._source: Live curve_sweep 2026-09-17 18:06, C220 @0.5s on the [AI] copy - the same frame as curveToe, channelToe and wheelBands. The BLUE curve's bottom point swept UP: its OUTPUT ([[0,y]]), which raises the channel's floor, rather than its input ([[x,0]]), which pulls the channel down. The direction the grade never had.
channelLift._model: CONFIRMED: out = 100y + v(1 - y), the mirror of the toe's (v - 100x) / (1 - x). Paired blue 7.8 -> 9.8 / 12.5 / 17.3 / 21.6 / 26.3 against 9.64 / 12.41 / 17.02 / 21.63 / 26.24 predicted - within 0.3 IRE on every row, and blue's own p1 tracks the same line (4.7 -> 6.7 / 9.4 / 14.5 / 19.2 / 23.9).
channelLift._freeHeadroom: THE POINT: a lift costs NO floor. floorRed/Green/Blue is 0/0/0 at every setting including y=0.2, and `readable` stays 100% throughout - a lift moves pixels OFF the floor, so the cast statistic gets more trustworthy as it rises, the exact opposite of the toe sweep (100 -> 80 -> 35 -> 5 -> 0). A toe spends the floor headroom the Master curve needs afterwards; a lift spends none of it.
channelLift._isolated: Isolated like the toe: pairedRed 10.2 and pairedGreen 8.6 identical on all six rows while blue goes 7.8 -> 26.3. About 0.93 points of B-R cast per 0.01 of lift on this frame.
channelLift._whyItMatters: Measured after the first live run of the black balance (C229 @9.42s, 17:59) fixed the blue blacks but left `black point 9.8 lifted`: red's toe hit its cap at 0.120, took red's own p1 to 2.0, and left floorCap 0.005 against the 0.02 levelsFor needs - so no black point was set at all. With both directions measured the level the three channels meet at is a free variable, solved jointly with the Master toe instead of assumed to be the lowest channel.

satRolloffBlacks._source: Live curve_sweep 2026-09-17 19:15, C220 @0.5s. The Luma vs Sat shadow roll-off written at depths 0.02 through 0.2 through satRolloff's own shape.
satRolloffBlacks._result: NEGATIVE, and worth keeping as one: it does NOTHING to the black end. luma p1 is 8.2 on every row and the paired bottoms are 10.2 / 8.6 / 7.8 on every row, unchanged to the digit; only red's own p1 twitches 9.4 -> 9.0 at the two deepest settings. So the roll-off is NOT the unmodelled 1.99 in the 19:11 black-point chain, and it needs no model for the black point.
satRolloffBlacks._note: Swept to 0.2 where the grade writes 0.35 (ROLLOFF_DEPTH). The trend is flat rather than shallow - zero movement, not small movement - so the extrapolation is safe, but 0.35 and 0.5 have not been read.

_blackPointResidual._source: The 19:11 chain on C229 @9.57s: 14.1 as read -> 11.2 black balance -> 9.58 curve 0.02 -> 9.01 sliders -> 11 read, MODEL OFF BY 1.99.
_blackPointResidual._ruledOut: Every write in the batch was measured against the black point on C220 @0.5s and every one is FLAT: Tint p1 8.2 at all seven values; the Highlights wheel p1 8.2 at all four hues; the Luma vs Sat roll-off p1 8.2 at every depth to 0.2 (satRolloffBlacks); the Master curve modelled to within 0.24 anchored or not (curveToe). Shadows moves p1 0.08 a unit and was at 2.06; Contrast +40 moves it DOWN about 2.9. No single write accounts for 1.99.
_blackPointResidual._conclusion: So the residual is not an unmodelled knob, it is model error carried from a ONE-CLIP calibration onto a different picture - the limit `_source` on every other block in this file already carries. The chain in the grade row now makes it visible per clip, which is the thing to read next: a whole-sequence run gives 18 MODEL OFF BY figures, and whether they share a sign says whether there is a bias to fit or just per-picture spread.

shadowsWheelLuma._source: Live curve_sweep 2026-09-17 20:26, C220 @0.5s - the same frame as curveToe, channelToe, channelLift and wheelBands. The Shadows colour wheel's LUMA slider, 0.5 neutral, stepped down to 0.25, hue and sat left at 0. The grade has never used this control; the skill rules it out as "the wrong tool showing".
shadowsWheelLuma._headline: It is a far cheaper black-point tool than the Master curve toe. For the same black point the clipping is about 20x lower: the curve at x=0.05 reaches luma p1 3.9 and puts 0.89% of blue on the floor, while the wheel at 0.4 reaches 4.7 for 0.04% and at 0.35 reaches 3.1 for 0.08%. `readable` stays 100% down to 0.35.
shadowsWheelLuma._shape: An OFFSET, which is what a colorist's Lift is, not a toe: at 0.4 the paired bottoms all fall by about the same amount (R -3.9, G -3.9, B -3.5) rather than being rescaled. The cast tightens slightly with it (blacksRB -1.6 -> -1.2 -> -0.8 -> -0.4), so it does not fight the black balance. Roughly 1.3 points of luma p1 per 0.05 of slider over 0.5..0.35, tapering below that.
shadowsWheelLuma._caveat: NOT free, and this sweep did not record the number: the wheel luma drags the MIDTONES. The 2026-09-15 `wheels` block has luma 0.4 -> p50 41.6 -> 38.4 on this same frame, so about 3.2 points of median for 3.5 of black point - nearly parallel, an offset on the whole lower range. The anchored Master curve exists precisely to avoid that (it is pinned at the median and at 0.8). So the choice is: the curve holds the midtones and clips, the wheel spares the shadows and darkens the picture. curve_sweep now records p50 and p99 on every row so the next sweep does not have to borrow them.
shadowsWheelLuma._openQuestion: Not yet wired anywhere. Before it is: does the median drag come back with the Contrast and Shadows sliders that run after it, or does it cost picture? That is a live question, not an arithmetic one.
shadowsWheelLuma._spacingCORRECTION:
CORRECTION 2026-09-17, from an independent review. `_castNeutral` says this control 'does not fix a cast' and that 'the channel curves own the spacing, this owns the level'. That generalises from C187, which is the one frame of three where it happens to be true. Measured paired red-minus-blue from neutral to x=0.25: C220 2.4 -> 0.8 (-1.6), C229 13.0 -> 9.8 (-3.2), C187 29.4 -> 30.6 (+1.2). It DOES move spacing, by up to 3.2 IRE, and the direction is frame-dependent.

THIS IS A SHIPPED INTERACTION, not a curiosity. bottomsFor sets the channel spacing at step 3 and shadowsLiftFor writes this wheel at step 5, with nothing re-reading the spacing in between. At the live C229 setting (x about 0.31 per blackEndC229._predictionCheck) it removes roughly 1.5 IRE of red-minus-blue - the whole of the NEUTRAL tolerance of 1.5 that the black balance was solved to. The lift is partly undoing the balance it is supposed to be completing. It is arithmetic and can be pre-compensated; it is currently invisible because the confirm render reads the total.

shadowsWheelLumaC187._source: Live curve_sweep 2026-09-17 20:5x, C187 (A056_05072025_C187.braw) at 22.02s, wheels verified neutral before the sweep. The SECOND frame this control has been measured on, and the first second-frame sweep of anything in this file.
shadowsWheelLumaC187._why: Chosen because its lowest channel is low and its bottom is a strongly coloured dark surface (paired R 41.2 / G 21.2 / B 11.8, cast -29.8). The open question was whether the wheel's soft bottom - it barely floors anything on C220 - survives when a channel is already near zero.
shadowsWheelLumaC187._answer: IT SURVIVES, decisively. Blue's paired bottom is driven 11.8 -> 3.1 and its own p1 10.6 -> 2.4, and floorBlue is still 0.01% at x=0.25 with red and green flat at 0 throughout. `readable` never leaves 100%. The control compresses toward the floor instead of stacking pixels on it. Compare the Master curve toe, which put 0.89% of blue on the floor just reaching luma p1 3.9 on C220.
shadowsWheelLumaC187._transfer: FIRST TRANSFER MEASUREMENT, and the model does NOT transfer cleanly. Across 0.5 -> 0.25 the luma p1 falls 6.6 on C220 and 9.4 here - about 42% more - so WHEEL_LUMA_P1 (a C220 table) under-predicts the offset on this frame. The PAIRED bottoms are closer: -7.8/-7.0/-6.2 on C220 against -7.5/-9.8/-8.7 here, all in the 6-10 band. Read as: the control subtracts roughly a fixed amount from pixels inside its shadow range on both frames, but where luma p1 sits in that range differs, so a p1-keyed table is the wrong key. This is exactly the one-clip-calibration limit, caught in the open.
shadowsWheelLumaC187._midtoneCost: Cheaper here than on C220. Median 55.3 -> 49.8, a drag of 5.5 for 9.4 of black point (0.59 per point), against roughly 1:1 on C220. C220's own median was not recorded in its block - it predates the p50 column - so the comparison borrows the 2026-09-15 `wheels` figures for that side.
shadowsWheelLumaC187._castNeutral: It does not fix a cast: blacksRB runs -29.8 -> -30.6 -> -31.4 -> -30.6, flat within the measurement. Confirms the division of labour - the channel curves own the spacing, this owns the level.

curveToeC187._source: Live curve_sweep 2026-09-17 21:0x, C187 (A056_05072025_C187.braw) at 22.02s, identity curves before and after, wheels neutral - so directly comparable with shadowsWheelLumaC187 on the same frame. The Master curve's bottom point, swept TWICE: `rowsPlain` is the two-point line, `rowsAnchored` is the four-point spline pinned at the frame's own median (0.553) and at 0.8, which is what levelsFor actually writes.
curveToeC187._anchorHolds: The anchor does what it is there for. Median 55.3 -> 53.3 anchored against 55.3 -> 46.3 unanchored, and p99 does not move at all (91.8 on every anchored row, where unanchored it fell to 89.8). An unanchored bottom point is a global stretch; only the anchored form is a toe pull.
curveToeC187._anchorDoesNotTouchTheBlackEnd: Floor and readable reproduce between the two forms within a rounding step at every x (floorBlue 0.43/3.02/10.96 anchored against 0.45/3.06/11.19 plain). Confirms curveToe._anchored on C220 from the other direction: the anchor is a midtone and top control, not a black-end one.
curveToeC187._vsWheelAtEqualBlackPoint: THE COMPARISON THAT DECIDES WHAT SHIPS, and it is not the one made on C220. Comparing at equal LUMA P1 rather than equal x (the two controls have different scales, so equal-x rows are not equal black points; wheel rows marked interp are interpolated between measured steps, not measured): luma p1 21.2 - curve x=0.1 median 54.5 / floorB 0.43 / readable 86, wheel ~0.43 interp median ~53.4 / floorB 0 / readable 100. luma p1 20.0 - curve x=0.15 median 54.1 / floorB 3.02 / readable 31, wheel x=0.4 MEASURED median 52.9 / floorB 0 / readable 100. luma p1 18.8 - curve x=0.2 median 53.3 / floorB 10.96 / readable 1, wheel ~0.36 interp median ~52.1 / floorB 0 / readable 100. So the anchored curve's midtone advantage is 1.1-1.2 IRE, bought with 3% and then 11% of blue on the floor and the cast statistic falling 100 -> 31 -> 1. On a coloured-bottom frame that is not a push-pull between comparable tools - the wheel wins on the merits, and the curve's only edge is inside the noise of what a median move is worth.
curveToeC187._reach: THE FINDING THAT BEARS ON THE CODE. The anchor costs black-point REACH: at x=0.2 the anchored curve reaches luma p1 18.8 where the unanchored one reached 14.1, and the wheel reaches 14.5 at 0.25 for 0.01% floored. levelsFor writes the anchored form and caps at LEVELS_CAP 0.25, so on this frame it structurally CANNOT reach a deep black point - the wheel is the only route there. Frame-dependent, not simply wrong: on C220 the curve reached luma p1 3.9 for 0.89% of blue, which is cheap. The difference is C187's low blue under a coloured bottom. So the allocation between the two wants deciding per frame from the predicted floor cost, which is the joint solve - and it is not written yet.
curveToeC187._paidInBlue: Everything the curve costs on this frame is paid entirely in blue: floorRed and floorGreen are 0 on every row of both sweeps while blue goes to 11%. The cost is not spread across the parade, it lands on whichever channel is lowest.
curveToeC187._castDriftOddity: No action, recorded because it is counter-intuitive. Unanchored, blacksRB runs TOWARD zero as it crushes (-29.8 -> -22.4); anchored it goes further negative first (-29.8 -> -33.7 at x=0.1) before easing to -31. `readable` collapses on the same schedule either way, so the value is untrustworthy past x=0.1 in both forms - but the direction of the artefact differs with the anchor.

blackEndC229._source: Live curve_sweep 2026-09-17 21:2x, C229 (A056_05072246_C229.braw) at 9.57s - THE FRAME THE PASS ACTUALLY GRADES on the proof clip. Pre-state verified clean on both calls (wheels the neutral triple, curves identity, no [AI] copy). `rowsWheel` is the Shadows wheel luma, `rowsCurve` the Master bottom point anchored at 0.53. Note the frame's own median reads 51.0, so levelsFor would pin at 0.51 and these rows are 0.53; the anchor held the median flat either way.
blackEndC229._wheelIsFree: On this frame the wheel costs NOTHING. floorRed/Green/Blue is 0/0/0 on every row and readable is 100 on every row, all the way down to luma p1 5.1. Not cheap - free. Its only price is the median, 51.0 -> 45.1 across the full range, about 5.9 IRE.
blackEndC229._curveCeiling: The anchored curve's honest ceiling here is luma p1 11.0 at x=0.05 - the last row with nothing floored anywhere. At x=0.1 blue is already 3.54%. So the wheel reaches more than twice as deep as the curve can go clean, for free.
blackEndC229._c220IsTheOutlier: THE GENERALISATION FAILS, and not in the direction expected. C220's ~20x figure does not transfer either way: on C187 the curve is three orders of magnitude worse than the wheel, and here the denominator is zero. At a matched black point of ~4.7-5.1 the curve costs 1.37% red + 0.02% green + 6.31% blue and the wheel costs exactly nothing. C220 - where the curve reached luma p1 3.9 for 0.89% - is the outlier of the three, and it is the frame every model in this file is fitted on.
blackEndC229._whichChannelPays: RED pays here, not blue - the opposite of C187, where red and green never floored on any row. C229's bottom is warm, so its dark pixels are red-dominant and the toe takes them first: red p1 hits 0 at x=0.15 and red's floor share overtakes blue's by x=0.2 (9.01% against 7.14%). So 'the curve pays in blue' is a C187 property, not a rule. A solver cannot assume which channel absorbs the damage; it has to read all three.
blackEndC229._castSignFlip: THE SHARPEST CASE OF THE readable DEFECT YET, and the reason castTrust exists. Cast B-R runs -12.5 -> -13.3 -> -14.1 -> -12.2 -> +4.3 -> +0.4. It CROSSES ZERO and lands at 0.4 on the row where luma p1 is 0.8 and 9% of red is on the floor. A verdict reading `rb` would rank that row the best-balanced setting in the whole sweep - better than neutral, which reads -12.5. On C187 the statistic merely shrank; here it inverts and actively recommends the destroyed frame. Pinned as a regression test.
blackEndC229._predictionCheck: The predicted post-fix black point of 6.6 for C229 is bracketed by measurement: the wheel reads luma p1 6.3 at x=0.3 and 7.8 at x=0.35, so ~6.6 sits near x=0.31 (INTERPOLATED, not measured), with floor 0/0/0 and readable 100 on both bracketing rows. contrastRule._source: Second-frame sweep 2026-09-17 21:2x, C202 (A056_05072128_C202.braw) @23.94s, ungraded (contrast 0 before, restored after), via the new slider_sweep tool on its first ever run. Compared against the `contrast` block, which is C220 @0.5s. `rows` is the C202 measurement; the RULE below is what the pair establishes.
contrastRule._theRule: CONTRAST IS A GAIN ABOUT A FIXED PIVOT: out = P + (in - P) * k, with P about 48-50 and k set by the slider alone. Two pictures with nothing in common agree on k at EVERY setting to within 0.016, and on P to within a couple of IRE:  -100 k 0.80 | -50 k 0.90 | -20 k 0.965 | 0 k 1 | +20 k 1.045 | +50 k 1.10 | +100 k 1.18. (The -20 pivot solves badly on C220 - 41.6 against 49.6 - because the move there is so small the two-point solve is ill-conditioned, not because the rule breaks.) This is a RULE rather than a fit: it is two numbers per setting that describe the control, not a table of levels that describes one frame.
contrastRule._whyItMatters: A table of absolute levels fitted on one frame cannot transfer, and this is the proof either way. The DELTAS happen to transfer for the parade ends - p1 within 0.4 and p99 within 0.4 across the full range, and spread within 0.4 (13.0 on C220 against 13.4 on C202 at +100) - so the statistic the pass actually steers contrast by was safe. But the MEDIAN INVERTS between the two frames: +100 moves it 37.3 -> 36.1 on C220 and 54.9 -> 58 on C202, opposite directions. A table says that is a contradiction. The rule says it is the expected consequence of a pivot: C220's median sits BELOW 48 so it falls, C202's sits ABOVE it so it rises. Predicted 35.5 against 36.1 measured, and 55.9 against 58 measured - right direction both times, from constants neither frame was fitted to.
contrastRule._codeImplication: src/grade_model.cjs predict() moves each tracked statistic by the table's own delta (or ratio where `scales`), which means on any frame whose median sits above the pivot it predicts the median moving the WRONG WAY under contrast. Not yet changed - the median is not what contrast is steered by, so nothing shipped depends on it, but anything that later solves the curve anchor or the body spread on a post-contrast prediction would inherit the sign error.
contrastRule._nextRules: The same treatment is worth applying to every other slider: find the FORM (gain about a pivot, pure offset, toe, and where its pivot or fulcrum sits) rather than banking a second table. Whites and Highlights should be a gain about a low pivot; Shadows and Blacks a gain about a high one; Temperature and Tint per-channel gains. Each needs one second-frame sweep to confirm the form and pin the constant.
contrastRule._DOWNGRADED:
CORRECTION 2026-09-17, from an independent review. This block called contrast CONFIRMED and it fails the very acceptance test this file applies to everything else. Median residuals on C202, predicting from a P and k solved on p1 and p99 alone: -0.53, -0.27, -0.22, +0.56, +1.07, +2.09. Signed and monotone, worst 2.09 IRE - WORSE than the 1.7 for which shadowsForm was downgraded to 'approximate'. Calling one confirmed and the other approximate was a double standard, and the error was mine.

Also withdrawn: '_whyItMatters' claims the median was predicted 'from constants neither frame was fitted to'. Untrue. P and k are solved from each frame's OWN p1 and p99 - two points, two unknowns - so the p1 and p99 agreement is zero by construction and cannot be evidence of anything. The median is the only out-of-sample statistic here, and it is the one that fails.

WHAT SURVIVES, and it is not nothing: the pivot structure predicts the DIRECTION of the median move correctly on both frames from the pivot's position alone - below 49.6 on C220 so it falls, above on C202 so it rises - which a table of levels cannot do at all. So contrast is an APPROXIMATE gain about a pivot near 49.6, right about direction, with a magnitude error up to 2.1 IRE at the extremes. Same status as Shadows.

whitesRule._source: Second-frame sweep 2026-09-17, C202 @23.94s, ungraded, via slider_sweep. Fitted against the C220 `whites` block.
whitesRule._theRule: WHITES IS A PURE MULTIPLICATIVE GAIN ABOUT ZERO: out = in * k. No pivot term - P solves to within +-1.6 of zero at every setting, inside the fit's own error bar (quantization is 1/255 ~ 0.39 and P's uncertainty is delta/(1-k), about +-7 at k=0.94). k by slider: -100 0.750 | -50 0.865 | -20 0.945 | 0 1 | +20 1.060 | +50 1.152 | +100 1.33.
whitesRule._outOfSample: k was fitted on p99 alone. p1 and the median were NOT used and both follow it: p1 10.87/10.6, 12.55/12.5, 13.70/13.7, 15.37/15.3, 16.71/16.5; median 41.16/41.2, 47.51/47.5, 51.85/51.8, 58.21/58.4, 63.26/63.5. Max residual 0.2 IRE. This is the cleanest form in the file.
whitesRule._clippingNote: At +100 p99 is pinned at 100 with 13.42% of red clipped, so k cannot be read from p99 there; the two unclipped statistics recover it independently and agree - p1 gives 1.324, the median 1.335. +50 already clips 2.74% of red, which is why the pass backs this knob off.
whitesRule._ITISEXPOSURE:
CORRECTION 2026-09-17, and it collapses two entries into one. WHITES IS EXPOSURE IN DIFFERENT UNITS: 100 Whites points = 1 stop, and both are a gamma-2.4 gain, which in display code values is the plain scale 2^(stops/2.4). Confirmed on TWO frames and across the whole range. On C202 the rows are bit-identical field for field - Whites -100 and Exposure -1 both give 10.6 / 41.2 / 63.5 / 72.9, paired 13.3/11/8.2, cast -5.5, sat 13. On C220, where the two blocks happen to sit on DIFFERENT frames, the measured gains still agree with 2^(pts/100/2.4) to within 0.007 at every setting - a stronger confirmation than same-frame, because the constant transfers.

So `_theRule` above ('a pure multiplicative gain about zero') is true but was never Whites' own property. The k table it records is 2^(pts/100/2.4) rediscovered.

UPWARD THEY SPLIT, AND THAT IS THE USEFUL PART. At the same requested gain, aiming both at p99 97.85: Whites +50 lands p99 97.6 - the clean gain, residual 0.25 - with max at 100 and 2.74/0.43/0.13% clipped. Exposure +0.5 lands 90.6 - residual 7.25 - with max 99.6 and NOTHING clipped. Same frame, same render path, same gain; one clips, the other rolls off. p1 is 16.5 in both and the cast is -8.2 in both, so they diverge only where the shoulder lives.
whitesRule._doNotRefit24:
A RESIDUAL THAT POINTS NOWHERE - recorded so nobody chases it. Against 2^(pts/100/2.4) the six C220 gains run -0.0040, -0.0073, -0.0016, -0.0042, -0.0064, -0.0055: all six NEGATIVE, at -100 and at +100 alike, a uniform measured/predicted of 0.9915-0.9983.

That uniform sign is what makes it uninteresting, and it rules out the two things it looks like:
 - NOT a wrong exponent. A gamma error biases gains above and below 1 in OPPOSITE directions, so the residual would flip sign across zero. Refitting confirms it: gamma 2.30 gives signs + - + - - -, gamma 2.50 gives - - - - + +, only 2.40 gives all-negative. And solving each end for its own exponent gives 2.357 from -100 against 2.435 from +100 - they straddle 2.4 and disagree, so no single exponent fits better than 2.4 does.
 - NOT a black pedestal. A pedestal biases ratio-derived gains TOWARD 1, which would read low above zero and high below. The signs do not do that either.

What is left is a uniform ~0.5% scale in however the gain was extracted - noise or quantization in the measurement, not a property of the control. KEEP 2.4.

One statistic-choice note worth carrying: these gains were taken from the MEDIAN, which runs 31 to 55.3 across the sweep and never approaches the ceiling. The same block's p99 reaches 99.6, and on C202 Whites clips 2.74% of red at +50 and 13.42% at +100 - so p99 is the wrong statistic for a gain at the top of this control's range, and any future fit should take k from the median or p1 there.

shadowsForm._source: Second-frame sweep 2026-09-17, C202 @23.94s, ungraded, via slider_sweep.
shadowsForm._theForm: APPROXIMATELY a gain about a HIGH pivot, and NOT exactly one. Solving out = P + (in - P)k from p1 and p99 puts P at 95-100 across the range (110.7 / 99.0 / 99.4 / 98.7 / 94.9 / 91.4) and p99 is nearly spared, moving 3.2 in total against p1's 21.1. So 'a gain about the white point' is the right first-order description - it is a dark-areas control, as Adobe calls it.
shadowsForm._whereItDeparts: The median is the out-of-sample check and it fails systematically, in a signed and monotone way: predicted against measured, -4.7 / -1.8 / -0.4 / +0.8 / +1.2 / +1.7. Nothing clips or floors on the positive side, so the +0.8 to +1.7 is real - the midtone moves further than a constant gain allows. Shadows is a band-weighted curve that a single gain approximates near neutral and departs from at the ends.
shadowsForm._aFalsificationDOWNGRADED: The panel's session offered a stronger argument - at -100 the median moves -9.0 while p1 moves only -7.4, and a mid value moving further than an extreme one on the same side is impossible for ANY gain about ANY pivot. The logic is right but it rests on the one row that is floor-contaminated (0.04/0.02/0.06% on the floor), and on every other row p1 does move further than the median. So the hard impossibility argument is not available; what stands is the softer, cleaner evidence above. Recorded because the difference matters: an approximate form you know the error of is usable, an impossible one is not.
shadowsForm._pivotWasIllDetermined: CORRECTION, 2026-09-17: the P of 95-100 quoted in `_theForm` is NOT well determined. Shadows spares p99 almost exactly (it moves 3.2 in total against p1's 21.1), which makes the two-point fit ill-conditioned in the same way it is outright degenerate for Blacks - see `_fitMethod`. The pivot number should not be used. What survives is the out-of-sample median residual in `_whereItDeparts`, which was doing all the real work in that fit, and the qualitative statement that Shadows is a dark-end control that spares the top.

castCoupling._source: Read off the C202 slider sweeps, 2026-09-17. NEUTRAL - what the pass calls a balanced parade end - is 1.5.
castCoupling._finding: THE TONAL SLIDERS MOVE THE COLOUR BALANCE THE WHITE BALANCE JUST SET, by more than the acceptance tolerance. blacksRB shift from neutral across each slider's range: shadows 4.7 (3.1x tolerance), whites 2.3 (1.5x), contrast 1.6 (1.1x). Saturation moves with them too - sat p50 runs 17 -> 12 under shadows and 17 -> 22 under whites.
castCoupling._orderConsequence: The pass solves the white balance and the pads FIRST, then writes the tonal sliders, and nothing re-checks the cast afterwards except the confirm render. On a clip where Shadows runs to +50 for a dark subject - which the 19:24 run did on four clips - that is about 2.7 of blacksRB moved after the balance was set, nearly twice the tolerance it was solved to. This is a real reason the corrections exist, and it is arithmetic rather than noise: it can be predicted and pre-compensated instead of discovered by a render.

_fitMethod._warning: THE TWO-POINT PIVOT FIT IS DEGENERATE FOR ANY CONTROL THAT SPARES p99. Solving out = P + (in - P)k from p1 and p99: if out99 == in99 then P = in99 satisfies the equation for ANY k, so the fitted pivot carries ZERO information and simply reports p99 back. Found 2026-09-17 by the panel's session while fitting Blacks.
_fitMethod._demonstration: Blacks returns P = 84.7, 84.7, 84.7, 84.7, 88.3 across its settings - beautifully consistent, and p99 IS 84.7. Reported naively that reads as 'a high-pivot gain with a pivot stable to 0.1', and Blacks is not a gain at all. Whites by contrast returns P = -1.3, -0.4, +0.1, +1.4, nowhere near either fit point, and is genuinely determined.
_fitMethod._rule: A pivot is only believable when it sits AWAY from both fit points. When p99 barely moves, fit the pivot from p1 and the MEDIAN instead, or abandon the pivot form and test a toe. And always check the form against a statistic that was not used in the fit - that is what caught Shadows, Highlights and Blacks.

blacksRule._source: Second-frame sweep 2026-09-17, C202 @23.94s, ungraded, via slider_sweep.
blacksRule._theForm: A TOE, NOT A GAIN, with an exponential length constant. The median moves 0.13-0.20 of the black point's move; a gain about the apparent pivot requires 0.427 (the median sits 42.7% of the way from pivot to p1), so it is under half at every setting. Fitting the decay from the three statistics per setting gives lambda ~ 23 IRE (24.7, 21.5, 22.8, 25.1, 19.7 across settings): the effect is down to about 5% by 70 IRE. The gain form is not approximately right here, it is wrong - its median residual (+4.8, +4.3, +0.91, -0.45, -1.2, -2.1) exceeds the median's entire range of movement (3.2).
blacksRule._theInstabilityExplained: THE YEAR-OLD BAN WAS HALF RIGHT. SKILL.md says 'lowering is not used automatically' after one run went 12 -> 1 on one clip and 12 -> 10 on the next. The cause is not the control - it is the LOWEST CHANNEL running out of room, and which clip that bites on depends on its channel spread. On this frame the floors are red 17.3 / green 13.7 / blue 9.0, and going down: -20 already has blue p1 at 0 with 2.09% floored and readable at 68%; -50 has 11.61% of blue and 1.53% of green gone with the cast unreadable at 1%; -100 is 21.62/9.80/3.31 with the cast null. Rate here is about 0.45 IRE of blue per slider point, so roughly -2 points per IRE of blue headroom - blue's 9.0 predicted the floor at -20, which is exactly where it landed. One frame, so treat the constant as indicative; the mechanism is not frame-specific.
blacksRule._upwardIsClean: And upward it is completely safe: no floor, no clipping, p99 fixed to within a quantization step across the whole positive range, monotone. It also IMPROVES the cast - blacksRB runs -7.1 -> -3.5 from 0 to +100, i.e. raising Blacks neutralises a blue-heavy shadow. So the most selective control in the set (0.13 on the collateral measure, four times cleaner than anything else) is safe in the direction the pass wants, and the ban belongs only on the negative side, as a per-clip cap taken from the LOWEST channel's p1 rather than a blanket rule.

highlightsForm._source: Second-frame sweep 2026-09-17, C202 @23.94s, ungraded, via slider_sweep.
highlightsForm._theForm: A BAND CONTROL CENTRED IN THE UPPER MIDTONES - not a gain, and NOT the Whites family. At +100 the median moves +12.6 while p99 moves only +7.8: a mid value moving further than the top is impossible for any gain about any pivot, and unlike the Shadows case this row is clean (floor 0/0/0.01, clip 0/0/0), so the falsification is sound rather than a floor artefact. It also holds at +50 (+6.7 against +5.1). The fitted pivot scatters 7.8, 4.3, -0.3, 1.5, -9.7 with non-overlapping error bars at the ends, and the median residual runs -3.4, -2.3, -0.9, +1.3, +3.4, +7.3 - signed and monotone. The band rolls off approaching 100, which is why max barely moves (97.3 -> 98.0 across the whole positive range). Downward the band sits higher: at -100, p1 -1.2, median -11.8, p99 -13.7.
highlightsForm._vsWhites: THEY ARE NOT REDUNDANT AND NOT THE SAME FAMILY, and the pass's habit of 'Whites first, Highlights to finish' is well founded for a reason nobody had stated. Whites is a pure gain about zero: it scales p1 proportionally and drives max into the ceiling (2.74% of red clipped at +50, 13.42% at +100). Highlights CLIPS NOTHING at any setting in either direction, and moves p1 by 2.0 across its whole positive range. Highlights is the tool that cannot blow the top out, not a weaker Whites.
highlightsForm._theCost: Per unit of white-point change, Highlights moves the midtone 2.4x as much as Whites: d(median)/d(p99) is 1.6 for Highlights at +100 against 0.67 for Whites at +50. So finishing the white point with Highlights after setting exposure walks the exposure substantially back out - which the pass does not account for.

exposureRule._source: Derived 2026-09-17 from the EXISTING `exposure` block - no new sweep. Found by an independent review pointing out that applying one functional family (P + (in-P)k) to every slider would mislabel this one.
exposureRule._theRule: EXPOSURE IS A GAIN IN LINEAR LIGHT: convert to linear with gamma 2.4, multiply by 2^stops, convert back. out = 100 * ((v/100)^2.4 * 2^stops)^(1/2.4). Predicted against measured on every downward row: -2 stops 6.2/20.7/48.2 against 6.3/20.8/48.2; -1 stop 8.2/27.6/64.4 against 8.2/27.5/64.3; -0.5 stops 9.5/31.9/74.3 against 9.8/31.8/74.1. Within 0.3 IRE on p1, the median and p99 simultaneously - and those are three statistics from a one-parameter model, so it is genuinely overdetermined rather than fitted.
exposureRule._upwardIsDifferent: Downward only. Upward Premiere applies a highlight tone map: the plain gain predicts p99 99.2 at +0.5 stops against 91.8 measured. The sibling premiere-map repo reached the same conclusion independently in its Round 250 - 'a plain gamma-2.4 gain downwards, a highlight-protecting tone map upwards, no static curve fits both'. So the rule is exact below zero and needs a separate tone-map term above it, which is not yet measured.
exposureRule._planImpact: This removes one of the five planned second-frame sweeps. It also warns against the fitting procedure the plan proposed: forcing a pivot-gain family onto every slider would have produced a bad fit here and reported 'no form' for a control that has an exact one.
exposureRule._notTheToneMapper:
HYPOTHESIS TESTED AND FALSIFIED 2026-09-17. It looked as though the upward roll-off might be the sequence's `autoToneMapEnabled` (true by default) rather than Exposure itself - which would have meant the offline simulator cancelled on 2026-09-15 was cancelled over a checkbox. It is not. A sequence-level tone mapper acts on the composited result and cannot know which slider produced a value, so if it were doing this it would roll Whites off too - and Whites at the identical gain instead puts 2.74% of red hard against the ceiling. The asymmetry is inside Lumetri's Exposure. handoff.md:388 stands, and no sequence setting was changed to establish it.

The roll-off is LEVEL-DEPENDENT, not a blanket compression. Measured/predicted at +0.5 stops: 0.985 at p1, 0.971 at the median, 0.926 at p99, 0.886 at max. Below about 20 IRE it is invisible even at +2 stops (p1 residual 0.34). That is a shoulder, and it is the shape a highlight-protecting tone map has.
exposureRule._whichToolToRaiseWith: THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PASS, and it is backwards today. Raising the white point with Whites CLIPS (2.74% of red at +50, 13.42% at +100); raising it with Exposure does not (nothing clipped at +0.5 or +1, 1.5% only at +2). Exposure is the highlight-protecting way to lift, and the pass refuses it upward while reaching for Whites. Highlights is the third and genuinely distinct tool - a band control that clips nothing in either direction. Downward the choice is empty: Whites and Exposure are the same operation exactly, so the canon setting both is setting one thing twice.
exposureRule._REVERTED_upwardTableIsRailed:
REVERTED 2026-09-17 23:56 after one live run. Routing the white-point lift through Exposure instead of Whites took the sequence from 5/18 balanced to 0/18, and the owner's eye said it plainly: over-exposed, inconsistent, flat.

THE CAUSE IS THIS BLOCK'S OWN UPWARD ROWS, AND IT IS THE TRAP I HAD WRITTEN DOWN TWO HOURS EARLIER. The C220 exposure sweep has max 91.4 at neutral, so every upward row is CLIPPED: p99 reads 85.9 -> 91.8 -> 96.1 -> 99.6, ratios 1.069 / 1.119 / 1.159 where the true gain is 1.155 / 1.335 / 1.782. The table records a railed response.

So the solver, asked to take a white point of 76.5 to 92, predicts +2 stops reaches only 90.2, asks for the range end, and the REAL gain of 1.78 takes 76.5 to 136 - clipped back to 97.6. Every clip with a low white point got two stops. That is the 'do not take a gain from a statistic near the rails' rule in `whitesRule._doNotRefit24`, violated by me within two hours of writing it, because I checked that Whites' table was clean and never checked Exposure's.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE: Whites and Exposure are the same control, and Exposure genuinely does not clip where Whites does - that was measured on C202, whose own rows are unrailed. The argument for the change was sound; the calibration available to execute it was not.

WHAT IT WOULD TAKE TO RE-LAND: Exposure's upward response must come from the FORM - the gain 2^(stops/2.4) with Lumetri's shoulder - and the shoulder is unmeasured (`_notTheToneMapper` records its shape at four points on one frame and declines to fit it). Measure the shoulder on an unrailed frame first, or drive Exposure through the forward model in src/forward.cjs rather than through the swept table. Until then Whites is the honest choice: it clips, and the pass knows it clips, and the damage guard backs it off.

whiteBalanceRule._source: Derived 2026-09-17 from the EXISTING temperature and tint blocks - no new sweep. The revised plan says to try the offline fit before spending a render; this is that, and it succeeded.
whiteBalanceRule._theRule: BOTH ARE PER-CHANNEL GAINS: out_c = in_c * k_c, one gain per channel, no pivot and no offset. TEMPERATURE runs red against blue (the blue-orange axis) - k at +100 is R 1.244 / G 0.935 / B 0.701, and at -100 R 0.760 / G 1.016 / B 1.337. TINT runs red and blue TOGETHER against green (the green-magenta axis) - at +100 R 1.295 / G 0.840 / B 1.298, with R and B equal to three decimals at every setting. That is the textbook pair of chroma axes, and it is what the measurements say rather than what was assumed.
whiteBalanceRule._overdetermined: Each channel's k was estimated three independent ways - from that channel's mean, its p1 and its p99 - and they agree to within 0.02-0.03 at every setting, which is inside the 0.4 IRE noise floor at these levels. A single-parameter-per-channel model matching three statistics is overdetermined, so this is identification rather than fitting.
whiteBalanceRule._whereItBreaks: Only where a channel rails. At temperature -100 blue's p99 estimate falls to 1.159 against 1.337 from the mean and p1, because blueP99 has hit 100 - the clamp, not the model. That is the single largest spread in either table and it is exactly the case the clamp model is needed for.
whiteBalanceRule._planImpact: This removes the last two discovery renders. All eight Basic sliders now have a form: Exposure (linear-light gain, gamma 2.4), Contrast (pivot gain, approximate), Highlights (band), Shadows (dark-end, approximate), Whites (gain about 0), Blacks (toe, lambda 23), Temperature and Tint (per-channel gains). What the C202 renders would now buy is confirmation that the CONSTANTS transfer, which is a different and lesser question.
whiteBalanceRule._overdeterminedCORRECTED:
CORRECTION 2026-09-17, from the second Codex review, verified. `_overdetermined` above says the three estimates 'agree to within 0.02-0.03 at every setting, which is inside the 0.4 IRE noise floor'. Both halves are wrong.

FIRST, the spreads are not 0.02-0.03 everywhere. Tint -20 blue gives 0.9412 from the mean, 1.0000 from p1 and 0.9382 from p99 - a spread of 0.0588. The worst case in either block is temperature -100 blue at 0.1827, which is the railing case (blueP99 reaches 100) already noted in `_whereItBreaks`, but Tint -20 is not railing; its p1 simply does not move (4.7 -> 4.7) and that is quantization at the bottom of the range.

SECOND, and this is the methodological error: a GAIN is dimensionless and the noise floor is in IRE, so the two cannot be compared at all. A gain uncertainty of 0.02 is 1.6 IRE at an input of 80 - four times the floor, not inside it. Gain error has to be converted to output units at the level it will be applied before it can be judged. commutation._source: DERIVED, not measured - 2026-09-18, item #15 of docs/color-sweep-queue.md. No render was spent and none is needed; revision 1 of the plan proposed a sweep for this and it is a two-line algebraic identity. Reproduce with `node tools/commutation.cjs`; asserted by test/commutation.test.cjs.
commutation._theIdentity: For two controls of the form f(v) = P + (v - P)k, the difference between the two orders is f(g(v)) - g(f(v)) = (kA - 1)(kB - 1)(PA - PB). The v terms cancel, so SWAPPING THE ORDER OF TWO PIVOT-GAINS SHIFTS THE WHOLE PICTURE BY A CONSTANT NUMBER OF IRE - it does not change the shape of the response, only its level. Verified exact (< 1e-9) against brute-force composition at every level from 0 to 100.
commutation._whitesXcontrast: Whites has P = 0 and k = 2^(pts/100/2.4) (`whitesRule._ITISEXPOSURE`); Contrast has P = 49.6 (`contrastRule`, APPROXIMATE - median residual 2.09, so every number here inherits that). Across the 36 combinations of +-20/50/100 on each: worst is whites +100 with contrast -100 at 3.355 IRE, then whites +100 with contrast +100 at -3.172, then whites -100 with contrast -100 at -2.513. 24 of the 36 exceed the 0.392 IRE noise floor - so the order of these two is NOT free at realistic settings, but it is COMPUTABLE rather than something to order around.
commutation._atRealisticSettings: whites -50 with contrast +100 = +1.274 IRE; whites +50 with contrast +50 = -0.771; whites -20 with contrast -20 = -0.095, which is inside the noise floor and genuinely does not matter.
commutation._whenItIsZero: A control at its neutral (k = 1) commutes with everything, and two controls sharing a pivot commute whatever their gains. Both asserted in the check.
commutation._whatItDoesNOTCover: PIVOT-GAINS ONLY. Blacks is a toe exponential in level and Highlights is a band; neither is of this form, so their orders are NOT settled by this identity and must not be assumed free. Temperature and Tint are per-channel gains about zero, so the identity applies PER CHANNEL with PA = PB = 0: they commute with Whites exactly, and with Contrast by the formula.
commutation._curveTOESareAlsoPivotGainsCORRECTION:
CORRECTION 2026-09-18, from a gpt-6-astra review, verified exactly (worst disagreement 2e-14 over x in {0.02, 0.1, 0.25} at every level). The first version of `_whatItDoesNOTCover` said the curve toes are excluded because 'their fixed point is at the TOP rather than at a pivot inside the range'. That is a distinction without a difference: A FIXED POINT AT THE TOP IS A PIVOT AT P = 100.

  toe  (v - 100x)/(1 - x) == 100 + (v - 100) * k, with k = 1/(1 - x), so k > 1
  lift 100y + v(1 - y)    == 100 + (v - 100) * k, with k = 1 - y,     so k < 1

THREE CONSEQUENCES.

(1) A toe and a lift on the same channel are the SAME control in two unit systems, exactly as Whites and Exposure turned out to be. They collapse to a single gain k about 100: use a toe when k > 1 (x = 1 - 1/k) and a lift when k < 1 (y = 1 - k). There is no reason to write both, and writing both risks an unnecessary intermediate clamp.

(2) The three channel toes share the pivot P = 100, so PA - PB = 0 and the commutator VANISHES. The measured three-way separability proof in `channelToe._isolation` - identical to the digit on six rows - is now EXPLAINED rather than merely observed. A measurement and the algebra agreeing is worth more than either alone.

(3) The identity DOES cover the toes against the tonal sliders, and the numbers are not small. A toe against Whites (P = 0) is 100(kA - 1)(kB - 1); a toe of x = 0.1 against whites +50 is 1.73 IRE, four times the noise floor. The order of the curve work against the tonal sliders is therefore a real effect with a closed form, not something to settle by taste. See `_curveVsSliders`.
commutation._curveVsSliders: Generated by `node tools/commutation.cjs`. Curve toe (P = 100) against Whites (P = 0) and against Contrast (P = 49.6), in IRE, constant in level. CAVEAT: this is the UNANCHORED toe. The Master bottom point as the pass writes it is ANCHORED and therefore piecewise - a pivot-gain below the anchor and the identity above it - so the commutator applies within the lower branch and the piecewise maps must be composed across it. The per-channel toes are unanchored two-point curves and are covered exactly.
commutation._andItIsUNCLAMPED: This is the difference between two unclamped maps. Once a channel rails, the orders diverge irreversibly and no closed form describes it. CLAMPING, NOT NON-COMMUTATION, IS WHAT ACTUALLY FIXES AN ORDER - this block bounds the reversible part of the ordering question and says nothing about the irreversible part.

Its quoted figures (-0.75 at whites+50/contrast+50, +1.27 at whites-50/contrast+100) are confirmed to the third digit by the generated table (-0.771 and +1.274); the difference is that the plan used a rounded k of 1.15 for whites +50 where 2^(0.5/2.4) = 1.1554.

curveToeAnchoredC187._verdict: MASTER IS NOT THREE IDENTICAL CHANNEL CURVES. Against OPS.masterToeAnchored(x, 0.55) on the x 0 levels: BLUE (the lowest channel) is on the line - 6.7 / 2.4 / 0 / 0 / 0 against 6.2 / 1.9 / 0 / 0 / 0, crushing where it should (1.44% at 0.12, 10.96% at 0.2). RED is 1.0 / 1.4 / 1.6 / 2.1 / 2.7 OVER the line. GREEN is 1.9 / 4.6 / 7.2 / 10.2 / 15.7 over: at bottom point 0.2 (20 IRE, above green's p1 of 19.6) the line says green crushes and it reads 15.7 with 0.00% on the floor. curveToeAnchoredC187._whatItMeansForThePass: Every prediction the pass makes through masterToeAnchored / predictLevels' anchored branch is wrong on any channel that is not the pixel's lowest, by up to the whole distance to the line. The black-point chain's 'curve N pixels' step and the chooser's Master candidates inherit it. The per-channel toes are exact, so a black point set with three channel toes would be predictable where a Master toe is not - but the channel curve is a 2-point line (gain 1/(1-x) about 100, no anchor: p50 54.9 -> 49.4 at Green 0.15), so it moves the midtones the anchored Master protects. shadowsWheelLumaForm._source: Derived 2026-09-18 16:40 from the two existing sweeps `shadowsWheelLuma` (C220 @0.5s) and `shadowsWheelLumaC187` (C187 @22.02s), no new render. Implemented as OPS.shadowsWheelLuma in src/forward.cjs. Prompted by the chooser's third live run, where every MODEL OFF BY above 1.2 (7.28, 2.9, 1.56) sat on a clip whose chain had a Shadows-wheel step - the one remaining control with no pixel form.
shadowsWheelLumaForm._theForm: The same BUMP family as the Shadows slider: out = in + ((0.5 - x)/0.25) * W(in), W a bell over INPUT LEVEL measured at x = 0.25, peaking near 20 IRE (-9.8), tapering to -0.8 at 91.8, and shrinking again toward the very dark end (-4.3 at 4.7). Linear in the excursion (0.5 - x): C187 reads 0.19 / 0.40 / 0.60 / 0.80 / 1.00 of the full delta at x = 0.45 / 0.40 / 0.35 / 0.30 / 0.25 - exact. C220 reads 0.31 / 0.58 / 0.74 / 0.91 / 1.00 - slightly convex at small excursions, but on deltas of 1.6-2.3 IRE where 0.7 IRE is under two codes.
shadowsWheelLumaForm._transfersCORRECTION: `shadowsWheelLumaC187._transfer` says the model does NOT transfer: luma p1 fell 6.6 on C220 and 9.4 on C187 for the same move. Both numbers are right and the conclusion was wrong. They were compared at luma p1, which is a different INPUT LEVEL on each frame (8.2 against 23.9) - and a bump moves input 8 by ~7 and input 24 by ~9.4. Overlaid by input level the two frames are ONE curve at every x: at 0.25, C220 runs 4.7->-4.3 ... 10.2->-7.8 and C187 continues 10.6->-8.2, 11.8->-8.7, 19.2->-9.8 ... 91.8->-0.8 with no seam. The control transfers; a p1-keyed table cannot, because p1 is not a level the control cares about. Same mistake `_transfer` half-diagnosed itself ('a p1-keyed table is the wrong key') without drawing the conclusion.
shadowsWheelLumaForm._heldOut: Tables built from x = 0.25 only; the rows at 0.45 / 0.40 / 0.35 / 0.30 on both frames are held out. C187: every statistic within 0.2 IRE except blue's bottom (-0.4 to -1.0) - essentially exact. C220: a UNIFORM-SIGN residual of -0.4 to -1.3 across every statistic and every interior x - the wheel moved C220 slightly MORE at small excursions than the linear amount scale says (its ratio at x=0.45 is 0.31 against 0.20 linear), where C187 is linear to the digit. Pooled median 0.56 IRE, worst 1.34, 51/60 within 1. NOT refitted: an exponent that helped C220 would break the exact frame, and a uniform-sign residual is the extraction/amount-curve disagreeing, not the level-bump being wrong (`_fitMethod`, rule 5). Same class of frame-to-frame disagreement as Shadows-down in `shadowsHighlightsForm._theAmountExponent`; a third frame settles which is typical.
shadowsWheelLumaForm._unswept: Only x < 0.5 (darkening) has been swept. The form refuses x > 0.5 rather than mirror it. The pass only ever lowers this luma (shadowsLiftFor), so nothing in production reaches the refusal.
shadowsWheelLumaForm._whyItMatters: With this, every control the pass writes to the parade's BOTTOM has a pixel form - the channel curves, the anchored Master, the Shadows slider and now the wheel luma. The wheel PADS (hue/sat) remain unmodelled and still drop the pixel context when they move.

highlightsPad._source: Live curve_sweep (pad mode, ab1b6a8) 2026-09-18 17:50 on A056_05072128_C202.braw at 23.94s, whole frame, fresh copy, clip confirmed to carry no Lumetri effect beforehand. Highlights wheel PAD at luma 0.5, hue fixed per sweep (QE: 0 red, 90 green, 180 cyan), sat 0 / 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.45 / 0.6. Rows carry every paired band level per channel (blacks, shadows, midtones, highlights, whites) plus channel p1 / p99 / mean. Nothing rails: worst clip 0.13% (red, hue 0, sat 0.6), blue floor 0.01% is in the baseline. Requested because the pads were the last control the pass writes with no pixel form.
highlightsPad._theFormIsAGAIN: NOT A BAND. The prediction was an additive bump over the highlights; the data is a PER-CHANNEL GAIN ABOUT ZERO. Per row, out/in is one number per channel across all eight level statistics, from the blacks (level 18) to the whites (88): spread 0.003-0.013, i.e. within a code. A bump would show a lower ratio at the blacks than the highlights and it does not. So the Highlights pad scales the WHOLE channel, blacks included - which is why a pad on a warm top was painting the blacks blue on 2026-09-17: a gain has no band.
highlightsPad._lumaPreserving: The Rec.709-weighted gain 0.2126 gR + 0.7152 gG + 0.0722 gB is 1.000 +- 0.006 on every row of every hue, and the measured luma median moves at most 0.8. A pad changes chroma and leaves luma alone, by construction.
highlightsPad._linearInSat: (gain - 1)/sat is constant per channel per hue. Hue 0: red +0.38, green -0.105, blue -0.105 (per unit sat). Hue 90: red -0.16, green +0.094, blue -0.405. Hue 180: red -0.39, green +0.118, blue +0.112. So gain_ch = 1 + sat * c_ch(hue).
highlightsPad._antisymmetric: c(180) = -c(0) to within 0.013 on every channel (this frame). CORRECTION 17:58: hue 270 was already on file - wheelBands.highlights, C220, sat 0.15 - and it mirrors c(90): from p99, c(270) = R +0.180 G -0.105 B +0.412 against the mirror prediction R +0.16 G -0.094 B +0.405. Both axes are antisymmetric. What the 0/90/180/270 rows do NOT test is the cos/sin MIXING at an off-axis hue - c(h) = cos(h) c(0) + sin(h) c(90) - and the pass writes pads at 29, 211 and 261. One sweep at 45 (and 135) settles it.
highlightsPad._whatItMeansForThePass: padsFor aims a Highlights pad at the WHITES cast and assumes the blacks are untouched; a gain touches them in proportion. solveCast's reach (PAD_REACH 12 at sat 0.3) is consistent with these rows (whitesRB -8.2 -> -19.6 at hue 0 sat 0.3), so the aim was right and the collateral was the surprise. With a pixel form the chooser sees the blacks move and can weigh it.

Asked because C227 @5.63s (pad 211.51 / 0.29) read MODEL OFF BY +1.6 on the sixth live run and its pad sat on the mirrored half of the table. Remaining candidates: the wheel-luma amount curve (C187 reads +1.5 deterministically at lift 0.30; C227 at lift 0.49) or the sliders on a frame that newly rails 4.7% high. Note for readers of the tool output: whitesRB is identical at 211 and 225 (-8.2 / 0 / +3.9) - that statistic cannot see hue; only the per-channel bands can. The panel's own reading compared 211 against 225 and called them different - true, and not the question; each must be compared to the table at its own hue.
highlightsPad._transfersACROSSFRAMES: The gain constants are frame-independent, measured not assumed. C220 (wheelBands, 2026-09-15, sat 0.15, from p99): c(0) = 0.387 / -0.105 / -0.105, c(90) = -0.144 / 0.070 / -0.412. C202 (this sweep, five sats): c(0) = 0.38 / -0.105 / -0.105, c(90) = -0.16 / 0.094 / -0.405. Red and blue agree to 0.02; green at hue 90 differs by 0.024 per unit sat, which at sat 0.15 and level 84 is 0.3 IRE - under the floor. The C220 p1 gains are NOT usable for this: p1 sits at 8-9 IRE where one code is 5%, and they scatter accordingly. Use p99 and the band levels.
highlightsPad._rowsNote: hue0/90/180 rows are complete tool output. hue45/hue135 rows carry the channel statistics and luma p50 only (the tool printed them in full; the record keeps the columns the fit uses). No row on any hue clips or floors above 0.13%.
highlightsPad._theHueTable: c(hue) per unit sat, least squares through the origin over every level statistic and every sat, C202: hue 0 = R +0.372 G -0.108 B -0.104; hue 45 = R +0.118 G -0.005 B -0.371; hue 90 = R -0.159 G +0.093 B -0.409; hue 135 = R -0.366 G +0.141 B -0.244; hue 180 = R -0.392 G +0.116 B +0.113. Luma-weighted sum within 0.008 of zero on every hue. Hues 225/270/315 are the mirrors of 45/90/135 - 180 mirrors 0 within 0.02 here, and 270 mirrors 90 on C220 (wheelBands) within 0.02, so the mirror is measured on both axes, not assumed.
highlightsPad._itIsAPlaneRotationWithAWarp: Fit each off-axis measurement to the plane spanned by c(0) and c(90): hue 45 sits at plane angle 49 with residual 0.009, hue 135 at 130.5 with residual 0.003 - so the pad IS one vector rotating in one plane. But the wheel angle is not the plane angle (a ~4 degree warp) and the vector length runs 0.39 to 0.46 with hue. A pure cos/sin model therefore misses by up to 0.033 per unit sat (red at hue 45) = 0.78 IRE at sat 0.3 and level 80, above the floor. The shipped form interpolates the measured table linearly by hue instead. Between measured hues the sinusoid curvature over 45 degrees bounds the interpolation error at about 0.02 per unit sat = 0.5 IRE at sat 0.3 level 80; the pass writes pads at 29, 211, 261 and never above 0.3 (MAX_SAT) except the nudge cap 0.5.
